Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Evergreen Utilities Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Evergreen Utilities Inc.'s Q2 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Strategy Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Technology Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Robert Hale, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, progress on our infrastructure investments, successful integration of our recently acquired Clinch River solar-plus-storage hybrid project, advancement of our Clean Energy Transition program, positive regulatory outcomes in Virginia, and enhanced community engagement in Loudoun County.

Rather than go into granular detail here, I'll highlight the key themes before turning it over to Lisa for the financial deep dive and then to our operating leaders. On the generation front, our fleet achieved exceptional availability amid weather volatility. Renewables expansion remains on track with major solar and storage additions. Cost discipline and infrastructure buildout are fueling rate base expansion, while the Clinch River integration has already added 25 basis points to ROE. Our sustainability efforts and regulatory wins in Virginia, including IRP approvals, are de-risking the transition, and community programs in Loudoun County have boosted local support for our data center expansions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss the financials.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. For the Q2 2024 quarter, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.50, up 12% year-over-year, and revenue of $4.5 billion, reflecting 9% growth. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $700 million, primarily focused on renewables buildout and grid modernization. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate EPS growth of 8-10% in 2025.

As we continue to execute on our long-term growth strategy, let me dive deep into our rate base growth outlook and the key assumptions underpinning it. Rate base remains the cornerstone of our regulated earnings power, and we're well-positioned to deliver consistent, multi-year expansion driven by disciplined capital deployment amid favorable industry tailwinds.

Our year-end 2023 regulated rate base stood at $28.4 billion, up 6.2% from the prior year, reflecting the successful in-service placement of $1.8 billion in capex, including the 300 MW solar-plus-storage hybrid project in our Virginia service territory and transmission upgrades in PJM. This growth contributed approximately 25 basis points to our consolidated ROE, with AFUDC accretion adding another 15 bps during construction.

Looking ahead, we project a compound annual growth rate of 6.5% for our regulated rate base through 2028, expanding it to $38.2 billion by year-end. This equates to roughly $2.4 billion in incremental rate base additions annually on average, with 2024 guidance at $2.6 billion—up 8% from 2023 levels. Post-2025, we see sustained 6-7% growth, assuming steady regulatory recovery of our capex program.

Primary growth drivers include renewable generation and storage buildout at 45% of incremental rate base. We're accelerating our clean energy transition in line with our Integrated Resource Plan approved by the Virginia State Corporation Commission and North Carolina Utilities Commission. Key projects include 450 MW of utility-scale solar in Virginia and North Carolina, leveraging Inflation Reduction Act Investment Tax Credits at the full 30% base rate plus up to 40% adders for domestic content and energy communities—yielding an effective after-tax cost of capital below 4%. Also, 200 MW of standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems in PJM, targeting frequency regulation and capacity markets, where we've secured provisional PPAs at $250/kW-year.

Transmission and distribution modernization accounts for 30% of incremental, with $800 million annual T&D capex including $400 million in 345 kV transmission lines across our MISO-South footprint to alleviate congestion for data center hyperscalers like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft. AMI rollout to 80% of customers by 2026 enables dynamic pricing and DER integration, with forecasted 2.5% annual load growth from EVs and manufacturing reshoring.

Thermal repowering and nuclear life extensions make up 15%, with $500 million in repowering our 1,200 MW coal fleet to 50/50 natural gas-hydrogen blends at Clinch River, and partnerships with TerraPower for small modular reactors adding 300 MW post-2028.

Customer-facing growth initiatives are 10%, underpinned by 1.2% weather-normalized load growth from EV infrastructure with 5,000 public chargers and data centers in Loudoun County representing 15% of new load.

Key assumptions include a constructive regulatory environment with 85-90% capex recovery within 12 months via general rate cases. We're filing our next Virginia GRC in Q4 2024 seeking a 10.25% ROE and 52% equity ratio. Inflation at 2.5-3%, 10-year Treasury yields at 4.0-4.5%. In PJM, capacity auction prices at $270/MW-day provide visibility. We prioritize growth-at-a-reasonable-price with IRR hurdles above 9%, funded 60/40 debt/equity, deleveraging FFO-to-debt to 16% by 2026.

This 6.5% CAGR positions us for 5-7% EPS growth.

Before moving on, I'd like to dive deeper into our revenue breakdown by regulated and unregulated segments, a key area of interest. For the quarter, consolidated revenues were $4.5 billion, up 8% year-over-year, driven by strong regulated rate base growth and robust merchant performance.

Our regulated segment accounted for $3.15 billion, or 70% of total, up 12%. Electric transmission and distribution contributed $1.95 billion, or 44%, up 14% on higher retail sales of 28,500 GWh, up 6% due to industrial demand. Rate cases in Ohio and Indiana unlocked $450 million annualized from grid hardening. Natural gas distribution $1.2 billion, up 9% on higher throughput.

Unregulated segment $1.35 billion, 30%, up 2%. Wholesale power $900 million, up 5%, with PJM capacity clearances yielding $250/MW-year, energy margins $45/MWh. Renewables and storage $450 million, up 15% on 1.5 GW additions, IRA claims $350 million.

Regulated grew faster at 12%, rate base to $45 billion up 7%. Unregulated hedged 70%. Guide regulated $12.5-13B FY24, unregulated $5-5.5B.

Next, our earnings per share performance and drivers. On GAAP, diluted EPS $1.28, up 16.4%; adjusted $1.24, up 15.7%, ahead of guidance. Revenues $2.45B up 8.2% on 28.5 TWh sales. Regulated sales up 9% on heat waves, new PPAs 1.2 GW. Merchant prices $58/MWh up 22%, PJM capacity $240/MW-day. OpEx up 4.1%, O&M savings $45M, fuel up 7%. D&A up 6% on capex. EBITDA $785M up 14.8%.

Northeast drove 55% uplift, West added from hydro/solar. Targets 50% carbon-free by 2030, FY EPS $4.85-4.95 high end.

On capital expenditure plan and project updates. FY2024 CAPEX $2.6-2.8B, up 12%, five-year $13-15B at 10-12% CAGR, 10-11% ROE.

Breakdown: Generation $1.4B (52%), renewables $650M; T&D $1.0B (38%); other $300-400M.

Projects: Sunbelt Solar Plus Storage 450 MWdc ERCOT +150 MW BESS, $650M, Phase 1 energized. Pioneer Wind 300 MW MISO, COD H1 2025. Harbor CCGT 650 MW PJM. GridFlex transmission 150 miles. Emerging tech hydrogen electrolyzer.

Tailored to ERCOT load growth, PJM capacity. Drives 8-10% EPS CAGR.

Finally, O&M expense management initiatives and efficiency gains. Q2 O&M $285M, down 12% YoY, $35M ahead. Predictive maintenance via Siemens MindSphere cut FOR 25%, saved $18M. Workforce optimization 10% efficiency, $22M savings. Supply chain discounts, fuel optimization $14M. Renewables O&M down 22%. Frees $75M FCF for CCUS, storage.

Now, over to Alex for operations.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Lisa. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas power plants due to the implementation of digital twin technology. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

Reliability metrics like SAIDI and SAIFI underscore our system performance amid grid resilience push. For Q2 2024, system-wide SAIDI 78.4 minutes, down 22% YoY from 100.6, below NERC 115. YTD 142.7, down 18%. SAIFI Q2 0.87, down 19%; YTD 1.62, down 17%. Saved $12M O&M, 2 cents EPS.

Trends: 28% SAIDI decline since 2022, fewer major events. Regional: Midwest 65.2 minutes, Northeast 168 impacted by storms but automation helped, California under 50.

Initiatives: ADMS FLISR restores 68% outages <60s, LiDAR vegetation cut SAIFI 31%, synchrophasor monitoring. BESS mitigated 27% ramps. $450M capex for hardened infra targets sub-70 SAIDI by 2026, $150M incentives.

These build our moat against liabilities, supporting EPS CAGR.

David Kim: Thank you, Alex. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the long-duration energy storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Southeast US market.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed zero-trust architecture platform to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting synchrophasor technology in our Virginia service territory.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our Integrated Resource Plan in Virginia State Corporation Commission. This will allow us to recover costs for new solar projects.

Robert Hale: Thank you, John. We are pleased to announce that our community outreach program in Loudoun County has resulted in a 25% increase in positive sentiment towards Evergreen Utilities Inc.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Lisa, Alex, David, Sarah, John, and Robert. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning team. I wanted to dive into your reliability metrics this quarter—specifically SAIDI and SAIFI—and how system performance is tracking amid the broader grid resilience push. Could you walk us through the numbers, any regional variances, and how your capex initiatives are playing into this?

Alex Rivera: Absolutely, Sarah, great question and timely as we head into peak summer demand. Reliability remains a cornerstone of our value proposition at Evergreen Utilities Inc., especially as regulators like FERC and NERC tighten ROE collars tied to SAIDI/SAIFI performance, and with data center loads from hyperscalers like Amazon and Microsoft ramping up in our MISO South and PJM footprints. [Note: Alex reiterates the full details already provided in his section for emphasis, covering metrics, trends, regional, initiatives as above.]

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from John Ramirez with Goldman Sachs.

John Ramirez: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter, team. Mike, you beat EBITDA guidance by 8% with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion, driven by strong thermal generation margins. Can you unpack the nuclear uplift and what you're seeing in forward power prices across PJM and MISO? Also, any color on the data center RFPs?

Mike Thompson: Thanks, John. Great question, and we're pleased with the quarter's results. On nuclear, our fleet—three uprated 1,100 MW units at our Prairie Island and Monticello plants—delivered a 15% YoY capacity factor improvement to 94.5%, thanks to our extended outage optimization program with Westinghouse. That translated to $250 million in incremental EBITDA from higher spark spreads, with realized prices averaging $45/MWh in PJM, up 12% from last year amid tight baseload supply post-coal retirements.

Forward power prices are robust: PJM 2025-2026 strips are holding at $38-42/MWh for on-peak, supported by load growth from hyperscalers. We've signed three 15-year PPAs totaling 1.2 GW with data center developers—two in Northern Virginia (PJM) and one in Ohio (PJM)—at blended $55/MWh fixed, with escalators tied to CPI. RFPs are accelerating; we're in advanced talks for another 800 MW, targeting closure by Q4. This aligns with our 20x24 strategy: 20 GW clean capacity by 2024, now at 18.5 GW with 1 GW battery storage additions.

Operator: Our next question is from Sarah Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Patel: Hi, team. Lisa, capex came in at $2.8 billion for the quarter, within guidance, but renewables deployment slowed to 400 MW vs. 600 MW expected. What's the story there, and how does that impact your $10-11 billion 2024 full-year capex range? Regional color on ERCOT and SPP?

Lisa Chen: Sarah, good to hear from you. Renewables deployment was paced by supply chain for our Bifacial TOPCon modules from LONGi and racking delays, but we're back on track with 1.8 GW added YTD across our 5 GW pipeline. Q3-Q4 will see 2.2 GW online, including our 500 MW Gemini Solar + 200 MWh BESS hybrid in SPP, co-located with existing gas peakers for FERC-approved resource adequacy credits.

Capex remains firmly in the $10-11 billion band: 45% transmission (grid hardening post-Uri), 30% renewables/storage, 20% nuclear life extensions (e.g., $800 million for Palisades restart prep), and 5% digital (AMI upgrades). In ERCOT, our 1 GW wind portfolio benefited from negative pricing arbitrage via 400 MW/4-hour Fluence Gridstack batteries, capturing $15 million in ancillary services revenue. SPP exposure is growing via our 300 MW Oklahoma wind farm, hedging against wind curtailments with 20% firming via gas dispatch. No changes to guidance.

Operator: Next up is David Kim from JPMorgan.

David Kim: Thanks. Mike, O&M expenses rose 7% YoY to $650 million, above our $620 million estimate, despite flat volumes. Breakdown there? And strategically, with DOE loan guarantees flowing to competitors like Talen Energy for Susquehanna nuclear uprates, any updates on your CCUS pilots or SMR pursuits?

Mike Thompson: David, spot on. The O&M increase was 60% labor—union contracts at our Midwest coal-to-gas conversions—and 25% from weather-driven tree-trimming post-Irma remnants, offset by 10% productivity gains from our Oracle Primavera P6 scheduling rollout. Nuclear O&M was flat at $12/kW-month, benchmarked against Exelon's fleet.

On CCUS, our $50 million DOE-funded pilot at the Cumulus Point 600 MW gas plant hit 90% capture rates on CO2 from GE Vernova's 7HA turbines, injecting into the Illinois Industrial CCS hub. We're scaling to 1 Mtpa by 2026 under 45Q tax credits. SMRs: MoU with NuScale for four 77 MW VOYGR units at a retired coal site in MISO, targeting 2029 COD with $2.3 billion DOE loan app pending. This positions us for IRA incentives and complements our 45% renewables, 30% nuclear, 20% gas, 5% hydro mix.

Operator: Our next question from Emily Torres with BofA Securities.

Emily Torres: Hello, all. Strong free cash flow of $900 million this quarter supports the $1.00 dividend hike to $4.20 annualized. But net debt-to-EBITDA ticked to 3.8x from 3.5x. Thoughts on refinancing the $3 billion 2026 maturity amid 5.5% 10-year yields? And EV load growth commentary?

Lisa Chen: Emily, dividend hike reflects our 60-70% FCF payout discipline, with AFFO coverage at 1.9x. Debt metrics: we issued $1.5 billion green bonds at 4.75% to refinance $1.2 billion legacy coal debt, keeping all-in cost at 4.2%. The 2026 tranche rolls via a $2 billion term loan at SOFR+125bps, locked pre-Fed pivot. Leverage stabilizes at 3.7x by year-end with $4.5 billion FCF guidance.

EV load: our California IOU peers like PG&E see 5-7% annual growth, but our Southeast exposure (SCE/Georgia Power overlap) projects 12% CAGR to 2030 from 500k chargers. We've invested $200 million in substation upgrades for managed charging, partnering with ChargePoint for VGI pilots yielding $10 million ancillary revenue potential.

Operator: Final question from Robert Hale with Citi.

Robert Hale: Quick one on guidance. 2024 adjusted EPS $5.80-$6.20 looks 5% above consensus. Sensitivities to NatGas at $3.50/MMBtu and any M&A chatter post-Vistra's $14 billion Energy Harbor deal?

Mike Thompson: Robert, guidance midpoint $6.00 implies 8% growth, with $0.20 upside from weather-normalized hydro (+15% output) and $0.10 from storage uplift. NatGas sensitivity: $1/MMBtu change impacts EPS by $0.15; we're hedged 80% for 2025 at $3.20 floor. M&A: opportunistic, targeting 2-3 GW clean assets in CAISO/MISO at 8-10x EV/EBITDA. We've passed on pricier Northeast nuclear but monitoring Talen-like CCUS plays. Back half accelerates with 600 bps FCF yield.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q2 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Evergreen Utilities Inc. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Evergreen Utilities Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
